relations.relationship: With Frederick Cooper, distinguishes identity as a political/practical category from the analytical processes of identification, categorization and variable groupness.
relations.evidence_note: Primary article opening pp. 1–2 and selected “In other words” / “Identification and categorization” section pp. 14–17 read in an explicitly identified OCR mirror. This is conceptual differentiation, not a dismissal of identity politics or all historical experience.

relations.relationship: With Cooper, analyzes the state’s power to impose classifications while distinguishing external categorization from people’s self-identifications.
relations.evidence_note: Joint primary pp. 15–17: state resources support official categories, but states do not monopolize identification and categories do not automatically produce homogeneous groups. Historical examples/referenced authors were not independently audited.
